text:
10 random notes/compiled thoughts on greeks, stoicism, eternal issues, why these books should be read, and a healthy dose of "nothing ever changes"

--

what matters: these books are 2000 years old and have been read by every single generation of conquerors, warriors, heroes, and emperors

the modern-day narrative or associated individuals are gnats on a dog's ass

I feel compelled to put some distance here in ur mind...to disassociate whatever u have linked

if someone is humping a genre, and then they turn out to be a goober, you'll associate the genre with gooberdom

its understandable but flawed

"oh, you read the same books as ivanka trump"

like, that's not a thing. although I suppose it is, given the triggering it caused. 

what happens if Ivanka Trump reads the Bible, does everyone convert to Zoroastrianism

anyway...they are great books that have done a lot for me, these are random/assorted things I wrote down, and the article is similar

these books will outlive every one of us, no one could ever tarnish the old masters

some old books are hard to read. these really aren't.

1. Man to man across generations - thoughts from exile

most are literally just a man dumping his brain out...usually in hardship or exile or prison or shipwrecked or watching their kingdom burn around them

Dante's Inferno, while he was banished from Florence...all the best books were written from periods of extreme hardship or strife.

Seneca's letters to Lucilius are the best, again, written during exile

frankly, exile sounds kind of dope

"you must go live by yourself somewhere in northern italy, near Lake Garda....or, perhaps Ios, maybe Mykonos."

twist my fuckin arm

It all shows u that nothing ever changes, they had the exact same problems we do

Same for Juvenal, Horace, all these guys were sickos

Poems about "This Consul is off at his country house, and so here I am, fucking his wife."

I think the Romans have eight different words for fuck, you fuck someone in the mouth, the ears, the ass, they were really innovating in terms of where a dick could be placed

I'd like to say that we've made tangible progress on stuff like Nero on Capri, pools of young boys that he called his "tadpoles," but clearly sex pests and remote islands are a timeless theme. The only progress is we decree "you die now" versus "you are the emperor of Rome."

The best material though is on hardship and adversity, they really said everything that could be said, and nothing in the last 2000 years has surpassed it (esp Seneca)

2.  No one’s opinion matters

don't worry about what everyone else thinks

I don't like Meditations, it has the best PR team or some shit, but there are 5-10 better writers, wiser men, and so on

I keep going back and reading it and its one of those books I don't get anything out of

Plus the cuck-related aura loss is hard to shrug off

You're the Emperor of Rome, you can't be having gladitors screwing your wife...not the meditations you want to have

but again - these books are so damn old

there is no current day insight to add on what should be read

I would highlight anything Epicurus, Diogenes, Plutarch's Moralia....Lives of the Eminent Philosophers by Diogenes Laertius is a big compendium

and then Montaigne is a scholar who doesn't just quote them, he goes double-platinum...puts an entirely new banger essay on top of a 1500 year old banger essay.

Most of these are free online.

3. Plato/Socrates/Aristotle are mostly boring

again, fuck everyone else's opinion

Republic is readable, Nicomachean Ethics is somewhat readable, the rest can be tricky

so don't feel like you're dumb

Seneca's other book, Dialogues I think, is a better second step

the only people who have really read these other authors are Philosophy PhD's, it's that kind of material

everyone else is probably LARPing or trying to big-dick you on some shit they haven't read

if you pick a book up, and it sucks, put it away and pick up a new one. the good ones will grab you.

but with all these books, I want practical knowledge I can use...if it doesn't fit that bucket, or it's not history like a Tacitus/Thucydides, I don't really need all the science or the proofs of God

A lot of Plato's books are that kind of stuff

So you can respect that he was a great thinker, influential, while also saying "maybe its for you, its not for me"

ignore the crowd, form ur own opinion

4. modern translations suck

the "modern" translations are not a panacea, we've had english translations forever that were fine...a boring book is boring, and flowery language doesn't fix the issue

it just feels doubly wrong, like reading Cicero translated by a liberal Vassar grad

No one hated "effeminate men" more, Cicero would have veto'ed this on sight... "what have u done to my Tusculan Disputations, you wretch?"

he's up there in the sky hollering at Zeus... "sir, please, one more thunderbolt for this author -- I'm calling for Marc Antony's head on a pike, and I sound like Jane fucking Austen."

"I can't, I just used my last bolt on the Daily Stoic guy"

5. Trace ideas thru time

even a cursory read shows you what ideas are eternal

this helps you see through a lot of bullshit

a "new" idea thats actually 2000 years old, but no one reads old books

systems of goverment, a lot of ways we do things are a work-in-progress and its possible we've gone backwards

after 4800 years of monarchy and aristocracy, to think that 200 years of democracy is the endgame...

or that "love marriages" are ancient.  those are like 100 years old, the other 5000 years we didn't do that

have to always contemplate these ideas that are taken as stable, we really have no clue what we're doing

the people were never fit to govern themselves, ever...there may have been a reason for that.

we can tell them they're ruled by Louis XIV, or we can let them appoint their own kings and get Sneako and Nick Fuentes. 

Plus, the fourth turning is due, it's time for the "lets try communist/socialist policies" cycle which happens every 80 years like clockwork.

"here's 94 countries that have tried it. the record is 0-94."

"interesting. well...maybe this guy from Uganda can get it right?"

every 80 years the people who knew shit died, and we start fresh.

6. tune out of daily discourse

everything is a "new" argument over something we never have had an answer to, shit that the Romans struggled with.

immigration, crime, punishment, corruption, inequality, freedom, liberty

crime and punishment might be the most ancient out of all these discussions...prisons are 4000 years old, haven't changed the Old Testament

neither has punishment in general, we're less barbaric in our legal system, but humans are still bloodthirsty beasts -- no different than the gladiatorial combat days

but once you see how little has changed, you laugh at the big-brained takes, from elon or anyone else

"what if we had more public executions" - tried that. people still did crime. 

"what if we built more prisons" - interesting idea. we've tried it for 4000 straight years, and it hasn't worked. and while i'm not Plato, I struggle to see how the rational conclusion is: 

"we should keep doing more of what hasnt worked."

"okay...what if we put the criminals into the prisons BEFORE they do the crimes?" 

that would make sense, wouldn't it? 

just as a sanity check....do you think that occurred to anyone, at any point, since 1500 BC?

also, there's a few books that go into how this would work...1984, Huxley's books, Clockwork Orange

how do you feel about the government having a livestream of your brain at all times, and you go to prison when they detect the urge for criminal activity?

doesn't sound so good, does it?

that's why nothing has changed since the technicolor cloak. 

7. the rich

a consistent theme since the romans and greeks is that politicians and goverment figures are disgustingly corrupt, and have always been the "true" criminal class

that part hasn't changed a wink

the amount of securities fraud charges that elon himself has found a way out of will make a good book someday

tweeting "we're going private, funding secured"....that is straight to jail

unless you're a trillionaire

the truth is Elon's tweets aren't about the justice system, they're his way of broadcasting, once a day, to the 250 million followers, on the global app that he owns: "FYI, I don't like black people."

he switches it up, a mug shot, a guy who reoffended, a black judge, a tweet on "don't let them tell you it's racism when you're trying to save America"

keep in mind some 80 years ago we still had lynchings and segregated everything

I don't know, I guess after you make a trillion dollars you don't transform into Winston Churchill

the man is just about chasing e-girls, ambien, k-bumps and apartheid, and having 20 kids with 20 different women

at some point he'll let slip that all this space exploration is "because I just can't stand stinky, smelly minorities."

and then just when you think he's living clean he blasts out a "PARTY ON DRUGS" at 2 AM

what does it mean?

it's not from Seneca, that much I can tell you

8. all the stuff people suggest we do to solve crime is on LLM's, its all in the greeks and romans.

you just have to ask "have we tried X, and what happened"

there is nothing we haven't thought of

keep in mind we tied 4 horses to each of your limbs just for the fuck of it, we drag bodies through streets on chariots

the rich and the poor alike continue to gravitate to crime

"what if we executed the judges?"

the judge sentenced them 10 years ago and hasn't seen them since. why would you execute the judge?

"because the judge didn't know, 10 years in advance, what the guy was going to do when they got out....hmm, okay."

see, these all come back to almost comically dumb assumptions

"the judges are freeing violent criminals!"

ok, lets think this one through together.

Federal judges are a group known for their love of anarachy and chaos and disorder, they hate rules, they ignore precedent, they love standing out from the crowd and they love taking career-ending risks for no reason.

the only person I've seen doing interesting, thoughtful work on this as a concept is John Arnold

beyond that, some of the older ideas from the Romans may be worth bringing back, the colosseum, men fighting for their freedom...we aren't any better morally than we were then, we'd still enjoy watching people murder one another.

what about a 32-team playoff, 3v3, and the winning 3 gladiators get hired to do investment banking rotational programs at Goldman Sachs

"what's your greatest strength?"

"I just murdered 94 men with a dull Gladius, a broken spear, a scutum, and my bare hands."

"hmm...okay, we can probably skip the questions on how D&A flows through the cash flow statement."

9. immigration

some argue that immigration was the primary cause of the empire's decline

too many Greeks showed up, the populace got soft and heterogenous and patriotism declined, barbarians at the gate showed up (the RJR Nabisco deal), and Rome became a hub for high-yield debt issuance

hold on, I might have that wrong... "hallucinated," some would say.

anyway, whatever the greeks/romans said on races and religions mixing, it's probably relevant

demographics have always been destiny

I'm not sure it's what I want to hear -- because there are definitely parallels to the west today, and I stubbornly believe "can't we all just get along" is correct, rather than "lets just go back to having one race per country" -- but I'll listen regardless.

this just another one of those issues humanity can't seem to get right

a lot of other daily news and debates, you realize are just like a tape stuck on repeat

"how can we solve abortion, guns, states' rights, prejudice," et cetera

most are the same ideas as 2000 years ago and the same sides being taken

and so reading old books, u lose patience for a lot of shit and a lot of people

u hear nonsense being spouted off confidently, paired with ignorance

"new" ideas that were discredited or disproved eons ago

keep in mind we haven't figured out if red meat is healthy or not...it's only 200,000 years old, or something like that.

you know what would be worth figuring out at some point, is "why can't people get a good nights sleep?"

mars is nice, I think people would rather sleep though

what about carbs? do we have an answer yet? good carbs, bad carbs?

have we figured out protein? red wine? where are we on orange juice?

the reason is that these have been co-opted by lobbies, so we've lost the plot...for most of the 20th century, "studies" showed that sugar and coca-cola were wonderful for you

and milk, which I guess stopped paying the PR bill/bribe

losing interest in this shit is a good thing.

10. Temporal dislocation/mismatch -- Move laterally thru history

on old books in general, we are subject to a mental time warp

1600's feels ancient

have to stop and think about, around 1600, when Montaigne was writing about Seneca

...the book was 1500 years old.

so don't just think "pre 1900 = ancient" or that it's a different era, even these 200-300 year jumps or gaps tell you that something is timeless

and follow writers and thinkers from one book to the next

if Montaigne references Seneca a lot, read Seneca

if Seneca refrences Epicurus, read Epicurus

TR read Coleridge, Napoleon read Goethe, everyone had their sort of "man to man"

there's something to that....find comfort in what they found comfort in

u dont need new sources/secondary material, I haven't read the stoic guy's books (and I support the popularity of the material so I generally support him), but its just not necessary

the old ones are readable

some stuff u need secondary material (like a Nietzsche), but the Stoics didn't mince words

END. Seneca on current events

one hilarious thing is that Seneca probably would have hated the daily stoic guy

very low tolerance for building a career off someone else’s words - the bill always comes due.

"Put something forth from your own stock." direct quote of his

he would've hated Taleb too, quietly letting credit accrue to his name that he knows belongs to antiquity

the old heads were not a fan of dickriders, and they hated critics.  some shit is timeless.

so, its always better to be original and wrong

mix ur own words and experience in there as u stand on the shoulders of giants.

given the choice, I'd MUCH rather people call me weird than unoriginal.

I'm watching this Bessent tweet get engagement, there's like 4 comments "wtf is wrong with you"

what, can't a guy enjoy a trifecta character assassination?  shit, Seneca and Cicero would have loved that...especially around the Second Triumvirate, everyone talked so much fucking shit

Bessent just speedran the Phillippics

"Ceterum censeo esse delendam Alex Soros"

--

Conclusion: be yourself, everyone else is taken.

take risk, write something new, or at least try to come up with something new.

no more "here's 90% other people, with 10% me peeking through the bushes"

every time you put yourself out there,

you always get two comments in tandem

1. "that's the best thing I've ever read"
2. "what the fuck is wrong with you"

that's how it goes

humanity doesn't need another "how to improve your life in 4.23 seconds"

it will benefit more from another Infinite Jest

1000 pages of straight up insanity by a twisted mind who then took his own life

we need more of those. I don't know if I want to read it again, but I remember 100-200 pages of it being, like....wow, I thought I was demented.

don't kill urself after though, life is too good.

ave atque vale⚔️
